name: NVIDIA Corporation
thesis: Sells the AI 'factory,' not just a chip. Fairly valued at spot - the edge is the entry, not the thesis.
bull: Best financials in large-cap tech: FY26 rev $215.9B (+65.5%), 71% GM, 60% op margin [FACT]
$120B net income, $103B operating cash flow, net cash [FACT]
Moat = CUDA + NVLink rack-scale + pre-booked CoWoS-L - three layers to beat at once [ATTRIBUTED]
2nd-cheapest in cohort (~32x fwd, PEG <1) vs AMD 181x, MRVL 103x, AVGO 66x [FACT]
bear: Gross margin already rolled 75.0% -> 71.1% (FY25->FY26), at the cycle top [FACT]
Inference (~2/3 of compute) leaks to custom ASICs at 40-65% lower TCO [ATTRIBUTED]
FY23 air-pocket proven: rev +0.2%, op margin 37%->16% in one year [FACT]
~43x trailing GAAP on a ~$5.1T base - law of large numbers bites [EST]
driver: NVDA's retained $ share of the accelerator TAM - CUDA/NVLink/perf-per-watt moat vs custom-ASIC inference encroachment, gated near-term by TSMC CoWoS-L + HBM supply.
valuation: ~32x fwd / ~43x trailing; PEG <1; 2nd-cheapest in cohort yet highest growth & margin. Base 75% share / $440B TAM = $244 / +5% IRR.
risk: A frontier model trained off-NVDA PLUS a structural sub-67% GM quarter and/or DC revenue growth <+25% -> flips to a paired underweight (put spread + long AVGO/ASIC), target $140-160.
footnote: Data on this project's mid-2026 synthetic clock - re-pull before live use. [FACT]=local SEC-XBRL/market brief; [EST]=modeled; [ATTRIBUTED]=third-party. Not investment advice.
